_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who have had an insufficient response to a previous treatment.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study with 24 weeks of blinded treatment followed by an open-label period; patients randomized 2:1 to WAYRILZ 400 mg or placebo twice daily, stratified by prior splenectomy and severity of thrombocytopenia.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with primary persistent or chronic ITP with unsustained response to IVIg/anti-D or corticosteroid, or documented intolerance/insufficient response to standard-of-care ITP therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Durable platelet response: weekly platelet count ≥50 × 10^9/L for ≥ two-thirds of at least 8 non-missing weekly measurements during the last 12 weeks of the 24-week DB period, absent rescue therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: 202 patients randomized and treated (133 WAYRILZ, 69 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Durable platelet response: 31 (23.3%) with WAYRILZ vs 0 (0%) placebo; risk difference 23.1% (95% CI 15.95, 30.31); p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were diarrhea (32%), nausea (20%), headache (18%), abdominal pain (14%), and COVID-19 (14%). Warnings include serious infections and hepatotoxicity/DILI.
target_moa: Small-molecule, covalent, reversible kinase inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK); acts in ITP via immune modulation including inhibition of B cell activation and interruption of antibody-coated cell phagocytosis by Fcγ receptor in spleen and liver.

rems.type: The DNH and DRM determined that a REMS is not necessary to ensure the benefits of rilzabrutinib outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was convened; the application did not raise efficacy or safety issues requiring external expert advice.

On June 27, 2024, the Sponsor requested Breakthrough Therapy Designation for rilzabrutinib for the treatment of ITP. The request was denied on August 26, 2024. Reasons for denial included:

requirement.text: 4878-3 Conduct a clinical drug interaction study to evaluate the effect of Wayrilz (rilzabrutinib) on the pharmacokinetics of P-gp, BCRP, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3 transporter substrates in adult healthy volunteers. The study will assess the magnitude of exposure change of the transporter substrates and inform appropriate drug interaction management strategy for coadministration of rilzabrutinib with these transporter substrates in adult patients with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia. This study should be designed and conducted in accordance with the ICH Guideline on Drug Interaction Studies M12 (August 2024).

requirement.text: 4878-4 Conduct a dedicated renal impairment study to evaluate the effect of severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min) on Wayrilz (rilzabrutinib) pharmacokinetics compared to subjects with normal renal function. The study will assess the magnitude of exposure change of rilzabrutinib and inform appropriate dosing instructions for patients with severe renal impairment. This study should be designed and conducted in accordance with Guidance for Industry: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function — Study Design, Data Analysis, and Impact on Dosing (March 2024).
